## Moderna, Inc. (CIK 1682852) — Primary Revenue Sources and Recent Trends

**Primary revenue sources.** Moderna is a commercial-stage mRNA vaccine company. Its revenue is overwhelmingly **net product sales of vaccines**, plus a small "other revenue" line (grant, collaboration, and licensing/royalty revenue).

Per the FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-12-31), net product sales by product were (in millions):

| Product | 2024 | 2023 | 2022 |
|---|---|---|---|
| COVID (Spikevax) | $3,084 | $6,671 | $18,435 |
| RSV (mRESVIA) | $25 | — | — |
| **Total net product sales** | **$3,109** | **$6,671** | **$18,435** |

Other revenue was $127M in 2024 ($37M grants, $48M collaboration, $42M licensing/royalty), down from $177M in 2023 and $828M in 2022 (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:428800). Total revenue was $3,236M in 2024 vs. $6,848M in 2023 and $19,263M in 2022 (fact IDs 2606798, 2606788/2606789, 2606779/2606780).

**How it is changing recently.**

1. **Steep contraction, driven by COVID.** Total revenue fell **52.7%** in 2024 (to $3,236M from $6,848M) after falling **64.4%** in 2023 (from $19,263M) — both calculated from the facts above. The 10-K attributes the 2024 decline to "a significant reduction in net product sales of our COVID vaccine," mainly lower volumes in Europe and the rest of the world as the market shifted from pandemic advance-purchase agreements to a seasonal commercial market (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:444800).

2. **Geographic mix has shifted toward the U.S.** 2024 net product sales: U.S. $1,726M, Europe $573M, Rest of world $810M — versus 2022's U.S. $4,405M, Europe $6,732M, Rest of world $7,298M (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:537600). U.S. sales were roughly flat year over year, but 2024 included an approximately $216M benefit from reversal of prior-year sales provisions; excluding that, U.S. volume declined on lower vaccination rates and increased competition (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:444800).

3. **Diversification is beginning but immaterial so far.** mRESVIA (RSV), approved May 2024, generated only $25M in its first partial year (sales began Q3 2024). Management describes 2024 as the year Moderna "became a multi-product company" and targets ten product approvals over three years across four franchises (respiratory, latent/other virus, oncology, rare disease) (chunks 1682852/mrna-20241231:19200 and :28800).

4. **Guidance and latest quarters point to further decline.** The 10-K states product sales "are expected to decline further in 2025" due to lower vaccination rates, fulfilled advance purchase agreements, and competitive pressure (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:446400). Quarterly revenue facts show $108M in Q1 2025 and $250M in Q2 2025 (fact IDs 2606799, 2606800), with Q2 2025 up 35.9% versus Q2 2024's $184M (fact ID 2606795) — a low-base comparison, not a return to prior scale.

**Caveats.** "Franchises" above are Moderna's own business-franchise language, not accounting reportable segments; the company reports a single operating segment. The 2025 quarterly figures come from 10-Q facts and are not full-year results. The bundled annual reports cover FY2023 and FY2024 only.

Other revenue was $127M in 2024 ($37M grants, $48M collaboration, $42M licensing/royalty), down from $177M in 2023 and $828M in 2022 (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:428800). Total revenue was $3,236M in 2024 vs. $6,848M in 2023 and $19,263M in 2022 (fact IDs 2606798, 2606788/2606789, 2606779/2606780).

**How it is changing recently.**

1. **Steep contraction, driven by COVID.** Total revenue fell **52.7%** in 2024 (to $3,236M from $6,848M) after falling **64.4%** in 2023 (from $19,263M) — both calculated from the facts above. The 10-K attributes the 2024 decline to "a significant reduction in net product sales of our COVID vaccine," mainly lower volumes in Europe and the rest of the world as the market shifted from pandemic advance-purchase agreements to a seasonal commercial market (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:444800).

2. **Geographic mix has shifted toward the U.S.** 2024 net product sales: U.S. $1,726M, Europe $573M, Rest of world $810M — versus 2022's U.S. $4,405M, Europe $6,732M, Rest of world $7,298M (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:537600). U.S. sales were roughly flat year over year, but 2024 included an approximately $216M benefit from reversal of prior-year sales provisions; excluding that, U.S. volume declined on lower vaccination rates and increased competition (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:444800).

3. **Diversification is beginning but immaterial so far.** mRESVIA (RSV), approved May 2024, generated only $25M in its first partial year (sales began Q3 2024). Management describes 2024 as the year Moderna "became a multi-product company" and targets ten product approvals over three years across four franchises (respiratory, latent/other virus, oncology, rare disease) (chunks 1682852/mrna-20241231:19200 and :28800).

4. **Guidance and latest quarters point to further decline.** The 10-K states product sales "are expected to decline further in 2025" due to lower vaccination rates, fulfilled advance purchase agreements, and competitive pressure (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:446400). Quarterly revenue facts show $108M in Q1 2025 and $250M in Q2 2025 (fact IDs 2606799, 2606800), with Q2 2025 up 35.9% versus Q2 2024's $184M (fact ID 2606795) — a low-base comparison, not a return to prior scale.

**Caveats.** "Franchises" above are Moderna's own business-franchise language, not accounting reportable segments; the company reports a single operating segment. The 2025 quarterly figures come from 10-Q facts and are not full-year results. The bundled annual reports cover FY2023 and FY2024 only.
